Backtracking line search preserving positive-definiteness

Source: R/ggm_layer.R
mc_spd_line_search.Rd

Given a Newton direction \(d\), finds the largest step $$\alpha = \max\{2^{-k}: k = 0, 1, \dots, k_{\max},\; \lambda_{\min}(K_b(\eta + 2^{-k} d)) > 10^{-10}\},$$ with \(\lambda_{\min}\) the smallest eigenvalue and \(k_{\max}\) given by max_halvings. The positivity test uses the numerical threshold \(10^{-10}\) in place of zero. Only positive definiteness is checked, not a decrease of a merit function. By Weyl's inequality, \(\lambda_{\min}(K_b + \alpha\,\Delta K) \ge \lambda_{\min}(K_b) - \alpha\,\|\Delta K\|_2\), with \(\Delta K = \sum_d d_d Z_d\), so an admissible step exists for small enough \(\alpha\) whenever \(K_b(\eta)\) passes the test; it may still lie below \(2^{-k_{\max}}\), in which case the search fails. The fitting engine of mcglm_graph calls the same search with 30 halvings.

Usage

mc_spd_line_search(eta_old, delta_eta, bases, max_halvings = 30L)

Arguments

eta_old

current parameter vector \(\eta\), with \(K_b(\eta)\) positive definite.

delta_eta

the Newton direction \(d\), of the same length.

bases

an object of class "mcg_bases" from mc_precision_bases.

max_halvings

maximum number \(k_{\max}\) of step halvings (default 30), so that at most max_halvings + 1 steps are tried.

Value

A list with components

eta_new

a one-column matrix with the last point tried, \(\eta + \alpha d\): the accepted point when the search succeeds.

step_size

the accepted step \(\alpha\) when the search succeeds.

halvings

the number of halvings performed.

is_spd

logical, TRUE when an admissible step was found.

When no admissible step is found, is_spd is FALSE, eta_new is the point tried with the smallest step, \(2^{-k_{\max}}\), which fails the test and must not be used, halvings is max_halvings + 1 and step_size is \(2^{-(k_{\max}+1)}\), half the step that produced eta_new.

References

Horn, R. A. and Johnson, C. R. (2013). Matrix Analysis, 2nd ed. Cambridge University Press. doi:10.1017/CBO9781139020411

See also

mc_check_spd

Other GGM layer: mc_build_precision(), mc_check_spd(), mc_precision_bases(), mc_precision_derivatives(), mc_precision_to_covariance()

Examples

b <- mc_precision_bases(3)
mc_spd_line_search(c(2,2,2,0,0,0), c(-.5,-.5,-.5,-.4,-.4,-.4), b)$halvings
#> [1] 0
